problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $\frac{3}{2}\,\text{kg}$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2},$
where $x$ and $y$ are measured in meters.
Find the moment of inertia of the plate about a line perpendicular to $D$ at a distance of $\sqrt{6}\,\text{m}$ from a parallel line passing through its center of mass.
worked_solution:
For a plane lamina of mass $M$ and a line ${l}_{M}$ perpendicular to the lamina passing through its center of mass, the parallel axis theorem states that the moment of inertia of the lamina about a line $l$ parallel to ${l}_{M}$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M,
$$

where $d$ is the distance between the lines, and ${I}_{M}$ and ${I}_{l}$ are the moments of inertia about the lines ${l}_{M}$ and $l,$ respectively.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=2\cdot 2=4\,{\text{m}}^{2}.$
Since the plate has a uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{(\frac{3}{2})}{4}=\frac{3}{8}\,\text{kg}/{\text{m}}^{2},
$$

and its center of mass is its centroid:

$$
(\overset{¯}{x},\overset{¯}{y})=(\frac{-1+1}{2},\frac{0+2}{2})=(0,1)
$$

Then, the moment of inertia about the perpendicular line through the center of mass is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{M} & ={∬}_{D}((x-\overset{¯}{x})^{2}+(y-\overset{¯}{y})^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}+3(y-1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{[3{x}^{2}y+(y-1)^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\int }_{-1}^{1}6{x}^{2}+2\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{[2{x}^{3}+2x]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(2+2-(-2-2)) \\  & =1\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about a line $\sqrt{6}\,\text{m}$ from the center of mass is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M \\  & =1+{(\sqrt{6})}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2} \\  & =1+9 \\  & =10\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
